settings.name_in_paper: Pure Exploration in Combinatorial Multi-armed Bandit
unmapped: Fixed-confidence identification of the optimal super arm (combinatorial pure exploration); each round the learner pulls a single base arm and observes its reward
Super arm set I subset of 2^[m] is arbitrary; access via offline maximization oracle
Learner uses |I| (or 2^m as an upper bound)
settings.definition_quote: The arms $i\in [m]$ are called base arms, and there is also a super arm set $\mathcal{I} \subseteq 2^{[m]}$. For each super arm $S \in \mathcal{I}$, its expected reward is $\sum_{i\in S} \mu_i$. ... At each time step $t$, the learning policy $\pi$ can either pull a base arm $i(t) \in [m]$, or output a super arm $S(t) \in \mathcal{I}$. The goal of the learning policy is to make sure that with probability at least $1-\delta$, its output $S(t) = S^*$.
A pure exploration problem instance of MAB is a tuple $([m], \bm{D}, \delta)$. ... we assume that all the distributions $D_i$'s are supported on $[0,1]$. ... we assume that the optimal arm is unique.

symbols.H_1c: width * sum_i 1/Delta_{i,c}^2, Delta_{i,c} gap between S* and best super arm containing (or not containing) i
symbols.q: algorithm parameter in [delta, 0.1] controlling number of sample sets

tuning: M = (1/q) log(12|I|^2 t^2/delta) sample sets, variance C(delta,q,t)/N_i

source.label: Theorem_Explore
source.quote: In the CMAB setting, for $q \in [\delta, 0.1]$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, TS-Explore will output the optimal super arm $S^*$ with complexity upper bounded by $O(H_{1,c}(\log{1\over \delta} + \log(|\mathcal{I}|H_{1,c})){\log{1\over \delta} \over \log{1\over q}} + H_{1,c}{\log^2(|\mathcal{I}|H_{1,c}) \over \log{1\over q}})$.

results.notes: Correctness and complexity hold jointly with probability >= 1-delta. Polynomial given the offline oracle. Remark 4.2 extends to delta in (0.1,1) by running with (0.1,0.1).

source.label: Theorem_Explore
source.quote: Specifically, if we choose $q = \delta$, then the complexity upper bound is $O(H_{1,c}\log{1\over \delta} + H_{1,c}\log^2(|\mathcal{I}|H_{1,c}))$.

results.notes: q = delta requires delta <= 0.1 since q in [delta, 0.1]; Remark 4.2 covers delta in (0.1,1).

symbols.H_m: sum over all arms (including optimal, whose gap is mu* - second best) of 1/Delta_i^2

source.label: Corollary_Complexity
source.quote: In the MAB setting, for $q \in [\delta, 0.1]$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, TS-Explore will output the optimal arm $a^*$ with complexity upper bounded by $O(H_{m}(\log{1\over \delta} + \log(mH_{m})){\log{1\over \delta} \over \log{1\over q}} + H_{m}{\log^2(mH_m) \over \log{1\over q}})$.

results.notes: Paper's m (number of arms) mapped to K.

symbols.H_m: sum over all arms (including optimal) of 1/Delta_i^2

source.label: Corollary_Complexity
source.quote: Specifically, if we choose $q = \delta$, then the complexity upper bound is $O(H_{m}\log{1\over \delta} + H_{m}\log^2(mH_{m}))$.

results.notes: Asymptotically optimal as delta -> 0 per the paper.
